sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Preserve the corrected applicability alternatives and upper-waterline ownership. Add the canonical calculation/path and table-selection terms needed to represent two separate UIWL and LIWL readiness calculations: each must use its corresponding lower/upper resistance input, both must use upperIceWaterlineLength and upperIceWaterlineBreadth, and each must produce its declared result term. Add explicit datatype/unit validation for maximumContinuousRatingPower, which is currently referenced only by SPARQL. Replace the current Ke table query with an exact, complete, non-overlapping Table 3-1 selection; it currently permits wrong combinations (for example, electric or hydraulic propulsion with fixed pitch can satisfy either value) and does not faithfully encode the conventional-propulsion table. sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair applicability logic. The top-level nltl:iceClass sh:in restriction makes the outside-class non-applicability branch impossible and falsely invalidates non-applicable ships. Remove that restriction (retain required controlled iceClass evidence), and replace the two non-applicability sh:sparql branches: SHACL SPARQL constraints conform when their SELECT returns no rows, so the current date<2003-09-01 and class-NOT-IN queries are inverted inside sh:or and can let applicable or inapplicable cases pass accidentally. Encode positive alternatives with SHACL Core constraints, such as constructionStageDate sh:maxExclusive 2003-09-01 and a sh:not wrapper around the applicable-class sh:in constraint, while retaining the applicable branch and all declared operand, relationship, result, datatype, and unit checks.

Do not attach upperIceWaterlineLength and upperIceWaterlineBreadth to the hasLowerIceWaterline node. Those properties belong to the upper ice-waterline owner, and duplicating them on the lower waterline targets the right properties on the wrong entity.
